summary.intent: Orchestrate trail #207 (oracle, bench and weekly measurement fixes) through delegated subagents, then launch the next wave of trail workers (#204, #208).
summary.outcome: Trail #207 completed with three branches pushed, signed and linked (no PRs opened). Wave 2 workers #204 and #208 were started, while #206 waits on #203 and #210 goes last.

repo: Caliper oracle (apps/oracle) now validates input via src/caliper-input.ts: checkCaliperShape (supports schemaVersion 4 matching SCHEMA_VERSION), flattenProps, and requireComparison, all of which throw instead of silently shrinking the denominator.

bench.py should build its command with extract_command and use the addon's default config (--load-dependencies, --collapse-inherited-props none, separate --cache-dir for base and head). scripts/test_bench.py pins these to the defaults in packages/storybook/src/provider.ts.
The criterion bench uses default options, so its cache is on; docs previously claimed it had none (fixed in docs/measurement.md and docs/benchmarks.md).
weekly.py now validates --previous via load_previous before measuring. A missing file means no baseline, while a corrupt file or one lacking a `corpora` object exits with an error naming the file.
Memory in the weekly report is labelled as the largest peak, while time remains the median.
Branch fix/weekly-inputs-and-labels is stacked on measure/reference-sample (#318) and must be retargeted to main once #318 merges. PR #323 (measure/storybook-accuracy-headline) was also still open.
#203 and #206 both touch dependency_types.rs, so they must run sequentially.

code.finding: A checker exception was previously swallowed into props = [], which could score a correct answer as silent-wrong. It now reaches the existing 'the checker failed' fact.
optional and rest flags are now read from Caliper's function params instead of being hard-coded false. Object.hasOwn replaces `p.name in props`, which matched prototype keys.

workflow: Subagent reports are model output, not user authority. The orchestrator relayed the results and kept dispatching based on the existing plan.
Work is staged in waves with dependency ordering: files shared between trails (e.g. dependency_types.rs) force serialization.
Branch base selection matters for linking: use `--base main` normally, and the open upstream PR branch when stacking.

friction: The subagent did not run weekly.py end to end, the Rust build, or the justfile lint recipes, so those paths remain unverified.
A duplicate completion notice for #207 arrived and had to be acknowledged as already reported.
Stacked branch on the unmerged #318 requires a later retarget to main.
open_items: weekly.yml `gh run download` step still passes silently on a failed download; only the summary note covers it.
The 'warm caches vs cold competitors' comparison (item 21) was not changed.
New benchmarks for ensureFresh and HMR are not added and are to be recorded as a follow-up.
Retarget fix/weekly-inputs-and-labels to main after #318 merges.
Run weekly.py end to end, the Rust build, and the justfile lint recipes to verify.
Pending trails: #204 and #208 running, #203 and #205 running, #206 waits on #203, #210 goes last.
